summary: Madeleine Biardeau was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She studied at the École normale supérieure de jeunes filles (~1943–1946) and the University of Kerala (~1953–1954), and was an enseignante at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).
Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as a professor at the University of Michigan, with his position attested in 1976 and from 2006 to 2009.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. Her career includes posts attested in 2012 at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhukar Anant Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and held professor roles at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1970, 1983, and 2026.

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky worked in Indology and history/archaeology after graduating in geology and chemistry from Fergusson College (~1947–1951). He founded the Archeology Research Group in Porbandar (1951) and served as Associate Director (1976–1996) at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Mahadev Govind Ranade was a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and other fields. He completed his studies at the University of Mumbai by 1862 and founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.
Mahananda Timilsina is an Indologist who earned a PhD from Nepal Sanskrit University by 2015 and later held a post at the same institution.

Mahasi Sayadaw was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Aletawya Sayadaw, U Narada, and Thelon Sayadaw. He was abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung (1941), resident teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (1947), and founded the Insight Meditation Society (1979).

Mahendranath Gupta was a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Hare School, Presidency College, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta (~1871–1875). Around 1885, he held posts at Surendranath College and as a professor at Ripon College.

Mahesh A. Deokar specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as Professor (attested 2011) and Head (attested 2020–2021) at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and as Regional Representative for the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, attested in 1882 and 1914.

Mahinda Deegalle studied at the University of Peradeniya, Harvard, and Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds, Wendy Doniger, and Diana L. Eck. He was a lecturer at Bath Spa University (~2002–2021) and held visiting roles at McGill, Harvard, and Colgate.
Mahiro Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021. He has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University (the latter attested in 2026).
Maho Iuchi works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Otani University by 2008 and served as a guest researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, attested in 2010.
Mai Mishiro is an active scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ryōmin Akizuki. His academic career includes professorships at Mie University, Rissho University, and the University of Tsukuba (~1983–2002), as well as serving as president of Toyo University (2009–2020).

Makio Ueno earned a PhD from Otani University by 2009. Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute (attested 2010) and Otani University as an assistant professor (attested 2012) and faculty member (attested 2022–2026).

Makoto Kitada is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed doctoral studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Kitada held a post at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2008–2010) and is attested as a base member at Osaka University in 2026.

Makoto Nagai was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1934–1942) and served as president of Chuo Shoka Junior College in 1951.

Makoto Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral coursework at Waseda University (~1994–2001). Around 2004, he held an assistant professorship at Komazawa University.
